newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Three Arabs hurt in West Bank clash.
newsitem.headline: Three Arabs hurt in West Bank clash.

text.p: Israeli soldiers wounded three Palestinians on Friday during a clash with 200 protestors over West Bank land, witnesses said.
Rafidiyeh hospital in Nablus said an ambulance had been sent to the hilltop site between the Palestinian village of Kufr Qadum and the Jewish settlement of Kedumim.
Hospital officials said two people who were wounded by rubber bullets had been treated and sent home. They said an Associated Press cameraman who appeared lightly hurt remained under surveillance.
They said the demonstrators were injured when soldiers fired rubber bullets to disperse them.
The Israeli army spokesman said it was unaware of any injuries.
Palestinian witnesses said the clashes erupted over Israel's construction of a road to connect five Jewish enclaves and an apparent attempt to expand Israeli settlements.
Bulldozers were at work and reporters saw settlers in a big tent on the site.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has promised to carry out Israel's international commitments to hand back West Bank land to Palestinians but insists Israelis have a right to settle the territory captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

The United Nations General Assembly is expected to adopt a resolution on Friday demanding an immediate halt to Israel's construction of another settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, captured along with the rest of the West Bank.
